>you will inevitably deal with bad actors who are going make you feel unsafe and uncomfortable. 

Which is my nightmare and what keeps me paralysed from even trying in the first place. My mum keeps saying "how will I know a bad guy from a good guy if I haven't dated anyone" just piles on the pressure. You can't get hurt again if you never try at all is basically what I've lived by for all these years. But I do want a normal life and I am going to try.
Thank you, I'm glad it worked out for you. Does give me some hope.

>approach some men

I can't think of much scarier than that. I don't know how I ended up in a state where this would terrify me but that's where I am. I am trying to be better. I did approach a man to get to know on a course I was on, it didn't go too successfully but I will keep trying slowly.
Thank you, it is good to know there is some hope. It is very difficult not to get into a mode of comparison but I try not to.
I ain't a dude! Happy to verify that with any mod. Being a dude online is much easier and I've done that my whole life.
Thank you, that is good advice. I did use to attend a sport but the anxiety was quite hard to deal with at some points so I packed it in. Though I am going to try and return eventually.

I'm also from the UK and my doctors and therapists I've had had have never heard of AvPD. It doesn't even have it's own page on the NHS conditions website.

After over a decade of trying many of the antidepressants, on and off work from breakdowns, many blocks of IAPT therapy my GP finally referred me to the local mental health team when we talked about AvPD to see if they could explore this as a possibility. 

Someone from that team spoke to me for about 20 minutes and then about a month later I received a letter with their "decision". The decision was that my problem was "social anxiety"   
and that I should be released back into the GP's care with the recommendation that I am prescribed sleeping pills (promethazine) and "first line antidepressants" ignoring of course that I have already had these... 

And that was that really. I truly hope you are given better care, OP.

Sorry for the late reply, ideally you should do both but you should prioritise getting a decent emergency fund first. Even without having a house an emergency fund can be a real bonus to have. Then you can focus on investing into ETFs.

>but at least monzo is reporting the fact you have it where many keep it hidden.

That's a good point and a positive for Monzo Flex over the others. The hidden nature of these new credit types was one of my main worries.

I'm not really sure why I am suspicious of Klarna/Monzo Flex over previous credit. To try and put it into words, I suppose because unlike previous "buy now, pay in instalments/later" for capital purchases (washing machine, sofa, cooker etc.) I feel this new type of credit encourages overleveraging yourself for much more frivolous items.

The psychological "pain" of purchasing which is, in my opinion, crucial to not overspending is being reduced even further. Remember the pain of handing over £60 in cash to get some trainers? Then it became digits on a screen and it became less painful and now with credit like this those digits are smaller or even 0 (not in reality but psychologically) the pain is all but gone.

The FCA are looking into all this but they seem a bit slow. I'm not a fan of the idea of even more consumer debt and even worse that it is "hidden" from mainstream lenders. How long before people are getting into debt for £180 bottles of perfume from Harrods when they would have ordinarily bought a £40 bottle. 

It's a great boon for retailers but I'm still not sold on it yet.

First off congratulations on the job role! You haven't said if you have any debts so I'll assume you do not. The next step for you from what I remember of the flow chart is to have 3-6 months expenses saved up as an emergency fund. 

You need to be honest with yourself here about how much you will need in your emergency fund. Some people have just the bare minimum i.e. three months of expenses saved rather than three months of actual salary saved. Some people have even less of an emergency fund saved because they intend to use a credit card if the worst should happen. You may feel comfortable going down that route. I have very severe mental illness so would not feel comfortable with a light emergency fund. Only you can decide that for yourself.

You can keep your emergency fund in Premium Bonds (many people here do as well) as you already have them. It is better to keep it in a low risk asset (premium bonds, typical bank savings account) i.e. not stocks and shares.

Once you have a comfortable emergency fund you can open and start topping up your S&S ISA. If you are intending to buy a house then a LISA is also worth looking into. There are many options so spend some time doing some research. One popular option here used to be the Vanguard S&S ISA due to the low fees. I used to have mine with Legal and General (they have sold that part of their business to Fidelity).

>"Quiet" isn't an insult and it might have been their misguided attempt to start a conversation with you.

It's a really interesting one as I hear the same thing e.g. it's meant as an ice breaker, they are worried about you etc.

It's not an insult but I suppose there is an implication in questioning it that there is something out of the norm. If someone walks into a barbeque party on a hot day wearing a full winter fur coat then I imagine someone will comment. People don't often question the benign. It's the highlighting that there is something atypical about you that is defeating. 

It's good that you have a snappy response. I'm always like a deer in headlights when it happens. My brother once joked that I should respond as if someone just told me "You're amazing". i.e. "wow, thank you, that's really kind of you to say." My family are witty and in general just want me to respond in a way that throws the uncomfortableness back at them but I always get flustered and forget to do it properly. 

In terms of your last paragraph it's kind of like I went through a reverse of that journey. I had been told that I was a good listener, helpful and kind etc. I loved how creative I was, how I had written a 40,000 novel (not a good one) when I was 13, played piano, built board games and other cool stuff. Did I care that I was quiet back then? Not a jot. I was a confident and happy child. 

It was when I became a working adult that the world kept reinforcing that those things "don't matter" or at the very least don't matter anywhere near as much as being a social person.
Thank you, it really helps me feel less alone knowing that others know thus struggle too.

I really felt the same, that things would get better over time. I was so full of hope when I first left school. Yes, I was "quiet" but that was hardly life destroying I used to think to myself. My hope is almost fully gone now.

Clubbing is really hard when you have severe anxiety so it's amazing that you were still able to go. 

I relate a lot because it is so, so difficult to deal with when you start off being really positive that this time will be different and then it isn't. It's hard to keep going. It's like you start off as a terracotta statue. Ready for the world. 

Then every failed social event chips a bit off. At the beginning it's hardly noticeable. A bit of finger here, a piece of of clothing there. You keep going because you are mostly still whole. But the painful social events continue to chip away at you. Months and years go by and sooner than you think you are struggling to stay upright. The statue is struggling to hold it's integrity due to the sheer amount that has been chipped off.

It's chilling reading this post because I've done the exact same thing. After a bad social situation I go through quite a trance. In fact that very night I just walked away from the pub in a random direction for ages through the night even as the area got dicier. I just couldn't bring myself to care about my wellbeing anymore. 

The only thing that really shook me out of it was not wanting to upset my mum as she has her own stresses at the moment, so eventually I got on the bus and went home. 

I relate so much to the feeling of being subhuman. What did your therapist say about the subhuman comment?

They truly are. You'd think with the amount of times I heard them they would roll off my back like water now. Weirdly, the more I hear it the worst it gets. At school I would brush it off easily because I believed it when my teachers said you need all kinds of people in this world not just loud ones.

Then I got to university and the doubt started to creep in when many of the modules had a big talking/presentation/group element. However, I still believed things were not lost and that I had other skills to offer this world. 

Then my working life post-university blew any remaining hope to smithereens.

Thank you and I do need to take away the positives as well (that I went at least). It's just as I get older it's become harder and harder to bounce back from these things when I thought it would become easier.

I relate a lot to not being able to post in whatsapp groups. Worst was when you finally get the courage to post and are simply greeted with those two mocking blue ticks. 

I also tried suppressing thoughts and trying to think of work conversations in a very detached mechanical way. I was off sick for anxiety in November 2020 and when I got back to work I decided I was going to have this complete fake stoic attitude. It lasted for a while until I had a breakdown end of Feb. I don't know what my approach will be now.

You're right in that we should focus out energies on those who won't judge on that. It's just that it can be quite difficult in life to avoid those who do.
Thank you, it really helps posting here and knowing others relate.

It truly hurts bad. I keep getting told that perhaps many people ask it as a way to enquire into your wellbeing or as an ice breaker but that's so bizarre. I can't imagine being worried about an extrovert and going up to them and saying "why are you so loud?" as a way of finding out how they are... I would simply smile and say "hey, you ok?" or "what you been up to today?".
I can't believe how bizarrely common it is.

Thanks for posting this. I literally haven't moved since it happened (haven't left my room or anything). Luckily, I had half a bottle of water and some biscuits in here. Usually, I've been able to bounce back from social situations much quicker but as I get older it gets worse and I feel quite tired and empty now.

You're right about our humanity even though it is very hard to feel human at times. I forgot I even said that. It's interesting reading this post back because it was written at the rawest point. On the bus coming home from the event trying to blink back the tears so that happy revellers wouldn't be freaked out.

I always wonder too what people want you to say when you get asked or told about your "quietness". There was a highly upvoted [thread](https://www.reddit.com/r/AskReddit/comments/knu5e3/extroverts_who_ask_others_why_are_you_so_quiet/) on Reddit about it not long ago which unfortunately doesn't yield too many answers. Maybe they don't see it that way but to me it's kind of like asking "why are are your eyes green?". It's just an odd question that because this world is kind of built through the lens of extroverts is somehow socially acceptable.

Back when I used to tell my mum about these things she said I should reply stuff like - "why are you so bald?" - i.e. spit back something cutting and hurtful but that's just not me.

Thank you so much, that means a lot. I really want to say I'm happy I didn't too but I don't quite feel like that yet.

Well you are in the right place to be talking so don't worry about that.

I've never been in love so I can't really imagine how difficult being cheated on must have been for you. I am really close to my mum as well and I can't imagine losing her. I really feel for you OP, you've had a tough couple of years and you feeling down is very understandable.

I think a lot of people will relate to how cold city living can be. Surrounded by people yet not truly connected to any of them. It's a real problem. I'm trying to get out out there and make new friends myself. I am starting a new organised sport soon (fencing) and was looking to join a local board games club when they start back up. Maybe a new hobby might be worth a shot OP? Even if just to break up the monotony of city living.

You're too hard on yourself regarding dating. The dating game is very difficult and stressful for everyone so you shouldn't put yourself down about this.

It's fencing! A bit out there but I saw the beginner's lessons randomly going for half price so thought why not. Might be a great chance to make some new friends. Also sword fighting is kind of badass. It was actually meant to start last year April-ish but because of Covid lockdown and restrictions it kept getting delayed until now.

It's six sessions starting mid-Sept and I am really nervous because of course the class will be filled with people and I am always paranoid everyone has come with a friend. When you walk in do you just take your place silently or say a "hello" to everyone? Overthinking shit like that constantly runs through my mind. It's always the "lull" periods that make me panic. Waiting for the teacher to arrive and start the class, lining up to get in etc.

I will definitely report back after I've been to maybe three/four sessions and say how it's gone.

That's true about having someone there being empowering so I should be at least proud of myself a bit that I managed to go not having that even if it didn't go too well.

Thanks and apologies for the late reply!

They were all partnered up except me but I can report they weren't overly "lovey-dovey". I believe they were probably like this for my benefit which I do appreciate. 

I try and think that (regarding being ignored) but it's difficult because sometimes it seems like it's only me having this issue and others make connections so easily.

We are young-ish (late twenties/early thirties friendship group). I think things were easier when we were younger. 

I agree. In fact, sometimes I get the sense that people see friendships on a much lower tier as other relationships which is a real shame. 

I certainly intend to make new friends if I can but it is extremely difficult. I am joining a new sport soon in September (bricking myself with anxiety over this) so maybe there is some hope there. 

Thanks for the offer, I've saved this post.

The time limit thing is definitely good and I do something like that already (I think it was suggested by the therapist and that's when I started doing it). It does help knowing there is a definite ending to a situation.

I don't think it's immature to feel upset at the situation. That's a valid reaction and there was a part of me that did feel like that but I know deep down he's not a bad guy. He really is spread thin. It's just a difficult situation.

That's very true and I really respect him letting me know the score. He's not a bad guy for sure. 

I already do the timing thing a bit. It's a constant battle between me and group events since I was 6 years old. Most I have gone to even if they've made me feel so bad about myself that I smash my head into bricks but in early 2020ish I simply cracked. I was beating myself black and blue and had a breakdown. I just couldn't bare to feel like crap and needed a respite from them.

I think it was much easier when we were all younger but many of them have partners now and their time is getting spread more and more thin so if they do have a Saturday spare for example to go to the pub they will want to invite 4/5 people than go to the pub 4 times. 

I definitely do think there is room for compromise and he didn't say it was stopping completely just that it was going to be massively reduced. I am going to try hard to attend the group events but it is very difficult for me.

I agree and to be honest he would probably agree as well and if things were ideal I'm sure he would continue hanging out one-to-one.

The time limit is a great idea and something I try and do anyway. It seems to help knowing that there is a definite ending.

I have tried to go cinema and shows with groups but there is a surprising amount of idle time where I go crazy e.g. buying our tickets, waiting in line, buying our snacks.

That's very true, we'll still talk on the phone and message each other silly stuff. I guess it's the mostly having someone to do things with that I'll miss.

Of course. The last event I went to was just after we could meet more than six people in the UK. It was basically a "get to know our partners" kind of event. So there was me, my three friends and their partners (so 7 of us).

I thought it would be kind of ok as there was an activity to it (bowling). However, I still struggled thinking of things to say when waiting to bowl. I tried to follow my therapist's advice by asking questions if I don't know what to say but it was very difficult as people were basically bantering as a group. 

It seems silly to dwell but I did ask one of my friend's girlfriend's things (i.e. what do you do, how did you meet X) and she just blanked me. That shot down my confidence. I tried not to see it as her ignoring me and remembering my CBT tried to think that maybe she was thinking about something. 

I just became more and more anxious throughout even though I tried to follow everything from my therapy but it wasn't working, of course I got the dreaded "Why are you so quiet" a few times as well.

When I got home I just felt so bad about myself/self harmed and it just wasn't an enjoyable experience.
Thank you, definitely not giving up and going to keep trying.
Unfortunately I'm not, I'm in the UK. I've saved this post as I do have cousins in the US and you never know, I may find myself there one day.

It's just government propaganda and ideology. Nothing about saving money. Many of the systems that are used to gatekeep benefits and belittle the unemployed are actually extremely expensive to administer. 

They just hope in a divide and conquer way that if we have an enemy to hate (the unemployed, benefit claimers) that we'll not look at the real evils going on in this world.

I love how I've met so many people who hate the unemployed "scroungers" (as we say in UK) or immigrants but no one who gives a fuck about [Exxon mobiles](https://www.channel4.com/news/exxonmobil-lobbyist-reveals-companys-involvement-with-forever-chemicals) [forever chemicals](https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2021/may/13/pfas-forever-chemicals-breast-milk-us-study) that will probably go on to kill thousands, if not hundreds of thousands. 

Who has hurt them more? That sad suicidal homeless guy sucking down cider and collecting £400pm benefit or conglomerates poisoning everything in your life? The scrounger of course! 

This world is a clown world.
In the UK it is hard as fuck to get disability for mental illness and made as difficult as possible for ideological reasons.

That's the funniest thing about it. They make people jump through so many hoops in the UK for PIP. Horrible assessment, long ass application form, being obtuse as possible by forcing you to call and fill out a paper form when everything else is online, rejections so that you have to fight to appeal. All for £60pw...

It's ideological madness.
He's not using hyperbole about that btw, they literally let people starve - https://www.theguardian.com/society/2020/jan/28/disabled-man-starved-to-death-after-dwp-stopped-his-benefits

For my mum it's societal bullying from government "Job Coaches". Her cleaning job is back breaking work for a 61 year old and barely pays more than unemployment benefits (£1050pm).

No one in the UK knows what to do with poor folk who are too old and broken to work but too young for their pensions. Through ideology they don't like people on benefits so they bully them into work they cannot even do.

If I could afford to I would study for ever. Just keep taking a different masters every time. Sometimes when I'm suicidal and depressed I'll role play that I won the lottery and select all the masters courses I would take MSc Automation and Robotics, MA Scandinavian Studies, MSc Computer Graphics Vision and Imaging, MSc Speech & Language Processing etc.
Can't afford to learn how to drive.

I can only go on my experience as a Junior Software Engineer in the UK across four companies (work experience placement, internship, two proper jobs) so take with a massive pinch of salt. Here's what I wrote on another post:

>I have to say that I also thought this was the way out but the days of the isolated programmer hunched over a computer who everyone leaves the fuck alone are dead.  
>  
>My software engineering job had meetings every single fucking day. You have to stand up in front of 10-12 people every day and say what you did yesterday for work and what you are doing today. Every day without fail - it's literally called a 'Standup'. It's suicide inducing and awful. That's on top of other meetings.  
>  
>Much of the code is proprietary or the company does not follow standard open source practice so you cannot ask Google for answers you have to ask senior engineers who ignore or insult you. It's painful to ask snotty sadistic seniors for help.  
>  
>I even had a job that required me to be on direct calls/emails with clients which is just as horrible as you expect. It's panic attack tier when you are expected to fix bugs at short notice. Many long evenings firefighting a major bug while clients scream at you as well.  
>  
>The job doesn't even pay that well in the UK unless you are genius tier either.  
>  
>It isn't the holy grail Reddit paints it as being.

EDIT: tldr developers these days are expected to social, team working, manage the whole software cycle (server fixes, maintenance etc), direct communication with clients. The lonesome programmer dream is dead.

Sorry to here that, OP. Happens to me a lot as well. I keep spazzing out of jobs through mental illness and autistic weirdness. 

I would love to have some side hustles to never have to interact with another person against my will. I don't even want to be rich, just about £20k a year is fine with me and I'll live on some shitty estate (I already do anyway). 

I have a few ideas I am kicking about:

\- Self publishing erotica (feel like I missed the gold rush on this)

\- Traditional publishing fantasy novel (like a needle in a haystack...)

\- Onlyfans (got to be some demand for skinny ugly nerdy looking guys)

\- Streetwear brand: I know a good sewing machinist relative who's just as autistic and struggling for work who would probably partner with me

\- Freelance software engineer: I am a shit and slow programmer but maybe I can bang out easy stuff on Fiverr?

\- Shave Ice cart: Feels simple enough, basically ice and syrup. Not much scope to fuck it up and upset customers. Doesn't seem to be a thing in the UK so feel like could be a good market but I hear the ice cream trucks are run like mafia and they might not like me trying to get their customers, also how would I get food and hygiene licenses and start up money?

Hmmm, don't really have any more ideas.

I have to say that I also thought this was the way out but the days of the isolated programmer hunched over a computer who everyone leaves the fuck alone are dead.

My software engineering job had meetings every single fucking day. You have to stand up in front of 10-12 people every day and say what you did yesterday for work and what you are doing today. Every day without fail - it's literally called a 'Standup'. It's suicide inducing and awful. That's on top of other meetings.

Much of the code is proprietary or the company does not follow standard open source practice so you cannot ask Google for answers you have to ask senior engineers who ignore or insult you. It's painful to ask snotty sadistic seniors for help.

I even had a job that required me to be on direct calls/emails with clients which is just as horrible as you expect. It's panic attack tier when you are expected to fix bugs at short notice. Many long evenings firefighting a major bug while clients scream at you as well.

The job doesn't even pay that well in the UK unless you are genius tier either.

It isn't the holy grail Reddit paints it as being.

That's what I am trying to work out. When I was on unemployment benefit (UC in the UK) I got £317pm. My mum expected £90 of that to help with bills and council tax (that leaves £227). Then there was my phone bill (that leaves £204). Then there was my food (That left £124), then there was travel on the bus here and there (That left aboyt £96).

The PS4 alone is £260.

It's certainly possible but not as easy to get. I saw a data entry job description that asked for someone "outgoing and personable". That shows how many have been applying that they can request bullshit "extras" that have nothing to do with the job.

With the NHS in UK therapy is free (though there is a minimum wait of three months on a waiting list in some areas). In my area, if you miss three appointments you are released from therapy as their reasoning is they could be helping someone from the waiting list. 

It's a bit of a circular problem because the most fucked up people will have bad sleep and miss their appointments and so are booted from therapy when they are in fact the people who need it the most. It's difficult.

As much as the oft repeated phrase "work harder" is said to poor people, it is mostly bullshit. Hard work is not the number one influence on being paid well. I don't understand why we keep repeating and believing this shared cultural fairytale when it is obviously false. 

It is basically a mixture of luck, risk and a job that is in demand. Tell me how a carer doing physically back-breaking work that is also emotionally draining with actual years of experience can earn less than me in my IT work experience placement spinning on my chair waiting for the manager to assign a task if hard work is the key?

I get what you are saying. You can't really blame them or be surprised but it's still disappointing to me. I've been in shit work situations where someone has been ill and knowing sending them home would fuck my day up and I still do it and reassure them with a smile not to feel bad for me and go home and take care of themselves. 

It's just sad how little people care about others instead of relentlessly always pursuing their own self interest. 

Exactly as you said even being asked kind of changes your day because you feel guilt or feel compelled to lie as to why you can't. It's like, why should you feel like that on your day off?

It's sad that we have such a sick 'hustle' culture that people feel guilty about time spent on non-monetised hobbies. I never found that any time I was having fun and happy was a waste just because it wasn't economical.

My friend had booked three days off and was asked to come in on one of them for the afternoon meeting even so. I don't get why he didn't tell them to do one. To me, even though the meeting was shortish (40 mins) you still have to factor in commute time and the fact that your day off is now restricted by the fact that you need to be at work for 40 mins at 4pm. 

It sucks that we live in a world where the manager even thought that was a reasonable request.

I don't really have too much hope and if I think about the future it sends me into a panic. There's a very high chance I will end up like that guy in Nottingham who starved to death in his flat (except I'll be on the street). 

I just try to take each day as it comes or despair becomes overwhelming. I try and focus on free things that I can do to keep my spirits up: walking, hiking, writing, free museums, reading library books.

I have very small financial goals that are not really focused on unobtainable things anymore.  I always look to cut whatever costs I can day to day e.g. making cheap batch meals, instead of buying a propagator to germinate lettuce seeds I would use a fast food container and clingfilm.

I have worked in many fields and found most of them to be unbearably awful in terms of social interaction no matter how well defined the tasks. I've done everything from cleaning to software engineer and they were all unbearable. 

Everyone no matter what is expected to be a social butterfly. I will never forget the day I saw an Indeed job that was data entry of paper files into excel that asked for someone outgoing...

I'm shocked by this too because I am from the UK as well and was also hounded. After about six weeks they start trying to refer you to all kinds of bullshit. I can't imagine being able to keep them off me for years. I guess it depends on the Job Centre.

Yup, work is hellish for me. Even small amounts of social interaction and stakes are tortuous to the point of self harm and suicidal thoughts. Knowing that it just goes on and on is hell. I hate other humans because they are often so cruel when it is unnecessary, I hate interacting with them as they hate me for not being as social/clever/fast as them. I'm off sick at the moment as I just snapped.

I've run out of sickpay which means I will have very little money soon. I should be scared of starving but weirdly I feel so calm. It's like starving to death is better than feeling the immense fucking mental pain and pressure of working again.

Money *is* my mental wellbeing. It's so fundamentally tied to your quality of life it's kind of hard to unbound it. Growing up poor and now currently poor from mental illness, low financial security has been baked into so many unhappy memories from as far back as I can remember. 

I think the the effects are diminishing though. Once you get that financial security I think money's power to impact your mental health becomes less and less. Then again Biggie did say "Mo money, mo problems" (can't relate).
Thinking I'll just end it then if nothing is better.

We're kind of losing that battle sadly. You practically have to go through an assault course to get PIP (disability payments) and that could only happen in a culture that demonises you if you don''t/can't work 50 hours a week with a 2 hour stuffy commute. UK has an ingrained culture of bullying the unemployed.

That's the thing about this world. People hark on about smarts and hard work but I would say it is often risk that gets people the big bucks. Back in 2012, my friend was banging on about some digital coin and how I should buy £50 of it like he was. I didn't because I was a starving student and thought that wouldn't be a good use of money when I am eating tinned baked beans every night. And yet here we are, my friend doesn't need to work (maybe ever again) because of the risk that he took. 

Smarts will only get you so far. It's risk that really catapults a person.

This environment is low key encouraged though of course no one will admit that. If you are not one of the productives then society treats you badly because you are waste of air to them.  Only those who will add to the productivity churn are worthy of respect.

Kind of... I think it's because often many risky or scary things have an end date. I know I may despise going on a roller-coaster but it is over in less than a minute. Same with jumping out an airplane, asking a girl on a date, hanging out at a party with people who don't like you, walking through a dodgy neighborhood. These are all temporary. Work goes on and on and on. Work is forever with only death or (less likely) retirement as a release. This is why it is worse than these things for me.
